title: Convoy TAMA-17, 29–30 April 1944
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · Coordinated attack group, Capt. G. E. Peterson

participants.name: PARCHE
participants.co: LCdr L. P. Ramage; pack commander Capt. G. E. Peterson aboard

paras.text: BANG's first attacks: four approaches on convoy TAMA-17 west of Luzon over the night of 29–30 April, with PARCHE and TINOSA closing in on her reports. Every mark is a position or attack typed into the boats' war patrol reports, beside the Japanese record of the same minutes, on one GMT clock.
Japanese loss list: Takegawa Maru (1,930 GRT) and Nittatsu Maru (2,859 GRT), both to BANG. No loss matches PARCHE's or TINOSA's attacks next morning; the rest reached Manila on 2 May.
Takao to Manila, sailed 1300 on 28 April. Its ships, as the escort division's table, Nittatsu Maru's movement log and combinedfleet.com name them, are in the convoy's own record: [[convoy:tama-17]].

Positions are the boats' own dead reckoning and star sights, and three navigators never quite agree, so the same convoy appears in slightly different places in each report. Lines between positions are straight; where a boat actually went in between is not recorded. Dashed outlines mark entries the report itself contradicts, kept with the reason.

BANG kept zone K (−10) and PARCHE zone I (−9); TINOSA kept zone H (−8) on station. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). On 29–30 April the target ship's own log and BANG's attack sheets agree to within one to seven minutes once both are in GMT.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (BANG 74802746, PARCHE 74828582, TINOSA 74856363). Nittatsu Maru's movement log and the 1st Surface Escort Division war diary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy lists and the 3–4 May sinking times from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

第十番船 (No. 10 ship) in Nittatsu Maru's log. Cargo not recorded there. She presumably sailed with the convoy from Takao on the 28th (J01); not recorded for her, so left blank. 1,930 GRT (J10)
救助擔任船トシテ武豊丸ト共ニ指定 (designated rescue ship together with Taketoyo Maru), Nittatsu Maru's log. Not in combinedfleet.com's list of the convoy (engagement luzon-strait-1944)
Destroyer. Departed Takao 1300 escorting TAMA-17 (J01); depth-charged BANG after Attack 1 and escorted Nittatsu Maru after the rescue (J06)
Destroyer. Sailed from Manila alone and joined en route on the 29th (J02)

paras.text: Takao to Manila, sailed 1300 on 28 April 1944 (the escort division's table). Only one ship's cargo is recorded: Nittatsu Maru loaded 250 t of coal at Takao to be landed at Manila (her master's log, p23). The other ships' cargoes and the convoy's arrival are not in the records read. BANG attacked it on 29–30 April; PARCHE and TINOSA were in the same fight against two convoys (engagement `luzon-strait-1944`, which says which boat attacked which).

The retired battle page listed thirteen merchant ships from combinedfleet.com. Ten are on combinedfleet's page for Nittatsu Maru (28 April: Kennichi, Kurogane, Belgium, Peking, Shiroganesan, Takegawa, Tsushima, San Luis, Wales, Yamahagi and Shirotae Maru, escorted by Harukaze, W-17 and the auxiliary gunboat Chohakusan Maru; Asakaze joined on the 29th), and are in `ships:` as secondary. Its Nissan Maru, and the Yashima and Hakka Maru that "other lists add", are on no page found, so they are left out. combinedfleet's Chohakusan Maru is the escort division table's Chojusan Maru (as read).
